page: Vultr vhp-8c-16gb-intel is a High Performance family server powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 350 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include a GPU.

Benchmark data positions this server primarily in the average performance tier for most standard operations. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1169.0 and a multi-core score of 6196.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 12523.23. Memory bandwidth is measured at 831.82 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 62.89 GB/sec for large-block reads. However, performance drops to the bottom 25% for multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (35.65 GB/sec) and PassMark database operations (2589.14). Large-scale workloads like medium-model LLM inference perform poorly, yielding only 5.01 tokens/sec for text generation.

Given its shared CPU architecture and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers a cost-effective option for workloads that require moderate compute density without dedicated core guarantees. It is well-suited for static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight text or image processing. It is less optimal for database-heavy operations or large-scale machine learning inference due to the observed performance bottlenecks in those areas.
